name: Dry Skin
description: Dry skin, also known as xerosis cutis, is a common condition characterized by a loss of moisture in the outer layer of the skin. It can affect people of all ages and may lead to discomfort, itching, and flaking.
causes: Use of harsh soaps or detergents
risk_factors: Use of hot water for bathing
Excessive use of soap or cleansers

daily_routine.step: Gentle cleansing in the morning and evening
daily_routine.purpose: Remove dirt and impurities without stripping skin of its natural oils
Lock in moisture and provide barrier protection
Protect skin from UV damage which can worsen dryness

natural_remedies: Aloe vera gel for soothing and hydration
lifestyle_tips: Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water
Use a humidifier in dry environments
common_myths: Using harsh soaps will help clean and deodorize the skin more effectively.
Exfoliating regularly can remove dead skin cells and improve hydration.
when_to_consult_doctor: If symptoms persist despite home care or if there are signs of infection such as increased redness, swelling, or pus.
prevention: Avoid excessive bathing and hot water

severity_levels.mild: Mild dry skin is characterized by occasional flakiness, itching, and tightness. Home care measures are generally effective.
severity_levels.moderate: Moderate dry skin involves more frequent symptoms of dryness, redness, and scaling that may affect multiple areas of the body. Professional treatments may be needed for persistent cases.
severity_levels.severe: Severe dry skin can lead to extensive flaking, cracking, bleeding, and significant discomfort. It requires medical evaluation and treatment.

expert_tips: Patch testing new skincare products before full application
Consulting a dermatologist for personalized advice on managing dry skin
